method: Information-design pass over every current ERIS web screen inventoried in brief-screens.md (53 screens incl. dialogs, panels and dead code), using brief-core.md as the only agreed facts: live DOM measurements (phone 375, iPad portrait 768, laptop 1440), the seven personas' top tasks and must-see/should-not-see lists, the first-day walkthrough friction (branch chief, coordinator, engineer, office chief, reviewer+admin), the vocabulary table and the per-area data-density verdicts (REMOVE/DEMOTE/PROGRESSIVE). For each screen the persona's primary task was fixed first; every data element was then classified as essential (visible by default because a top task needs it to decide or act), secondary (available on demand with an exact placement: expandable row, details drawer or bottom sheet, hover/long-press with an always-visible fallback, 'More' tab, overflow menu, confirm sheet) or hidden/removed (duplicate, raw code, internal id, page-local KPI, dead code). Column budgets follow the responsive-table ladder in brief-research.md (card rows below 600px, prioritised columns 600-1199px, full table >=1200px, max 6-7 columns, one status per row, location as a single string, 44px targets on coarse pointers). Field availability was verified against web/src/api/types.ts, web/src/api/assessments.ts and web/src/features/eventGroups/eventGroupTypes.ts; where a needed value is not in the API (reporter name, submission creator name, WorkflowEvent actor name, office_name on Assessment, incident photo list, per-incident assessment id on Event Group detail) the item says 'flag: backend' instead of inventing it. Backend objects and the state machine are unchanged; UI labels map 1:1 to Incident, Event Group, Assessment, Submission (technical submission) and the canonical roles.

globalRules: One name per object everywhere on the web: Incident (report), Event Group, Assessment, Technical submission, Review; never GISA, Project (except 'Cross-section project'), Case, ticket or 'submission' for the act of submitting.

Never render raw enum codes, state codes, stage codes, event types, role codes, office codes, section keys or MIME types as user text; every code passes through one label map (roleLabel, assessmentStateLabel, submissionStatusLabel, incidentWorkflowLabel, eventTypeLabel, officeLabel, sectionLabel). REJECTED is shown as 'Returned for correction'.

One status per object per row: an incident shows a single 'Workflow position' label derived from current_stage + status + location_match_status + triage_disposition; an assessment shows its state; a technical submission shows its status. Never show status and stage side by side.

Internal ids (Incident #, Assessment #, Submission #, User #, Dataset #, attachment #, UUIDs) are never primary text; they trail the human key as muted text or live in a details drawer. incident_key is the incident's human key once minted. Never show 'User #7': omit the value until the API supplies a name (flag backend).

Location is always one string from one helper: 'District 7 · Los Angeles · Route 101 · PM 12.30' (district, county, route, post_mile), never four separate fields or 'D7 · R101' abbreviations in the UI; coordinates are secondary (details, copy button, map) and never appear in list rows.

Timestamps are relative by default ('3 days ago', 'Updated 6 min ago') with the absolute date-time on hover/long-press and in detail views; never raw ISO strings, never seconds; queue and record rows carry an age ('in this step 6 days').

Counts appear only where they are actionable: nav badges for items waiting on me, group headers, filter chips with true server totals, table captions ('Showing 50 of 1,240'). No page-local KPI cards computed from the loaded page, and never the same count twice on one screen.

Names, not codes, for people and places: full_name (email only to disambiguate duplicates), office name ('North GeoTech Office'), 'District 7', 'Route 101'; 'Waiting on you' when the viewer owns the step, otherwise the humanised role and person.
Place before ids: any row or card describing an incident, assessment or submission leads with the incident title and location string, then status, then age; ids last.

Column budget: below 600px every list is a card list (2-3 lines, whole row is the target, 44px min height); 600-1199px a table with at most 4 prioritised columns plus a trailing action and an expandable row; >=1200px at most 6 columns plus one row action; numeric columns right-aligned; column pickers instead of horizontal scroll for primary tables.

Progressive disclosure has three tiers and only those: secondary content goes to an expandable row, a details drawer/bottom sheet, a hover/long-press tooltip with an always-visible fallback, an overflow ('…') menu, or a 'More' tab; never nest disclosure more than two levels; never put essential information (units, requirements, status meaning) in hover-only tooltips.

Every screen gets one primary action per role/state, placed where the decision is read (Next step card, sticky action bar); irreversible or notifying actions open a confirm sheet that names the target and consequence and holds that action's optional note; every action ends with a persistent success notice naming what happened.

Maps appear at most once per screen and never inside list rows; below 840px a map and its list are separated by a sticky 'Map | List' control or the map is a secondary tab; map heights are viewport-relative (clamp), popups dock below 768px, and markers encode status by shape + colour + label. The global .esri-view class never receives position or z-index.

Empty states have three tiers: skeleton while loading (never flash 'No results'), teaching empty ('No reports need your decision. New field reports appear here automatically.' + one action), and filtered-empty ('No open Event Groups match "x" - Search all Event Groups').

Forms are single-column (max 640-720px measure); labels always visible; units as suffixes outside the input with inputmode=decimal; tri-state questions are radios with no default; validation on section-complete/submit with inline messages and a linked error summary; drafts autosave with a visible 'Draft saved 14:32' chip and a leave-page guard.

Role-gated content is not rendered at all for roles that cannot act on it (no disabled admin controls for coordinators, no Event Group links for reporters, no assessment column for maintenance-only users); read-only views render values, not disabled inputs.

Duplicates are removed, not demoted: no eyebrow that restates a title, no header card that restates the h1 and its buttons, no second back button beside a breadcrumb, no organisational taglines or copyright inside the app frame.

Colour never carries meaning alone: badges pair colour with text (and optional icon), selected chips carry aria-pressed and a check glyph, current pipeline step carries aria-current; contrast >= 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for badges and map symbols; 24px minimum targets everywhere and 44px under @media (pointer: coarse).

Dead code is deleted, not redesigned: legacy Projects pages, ProjectAssociationDialog, the unused MissionCenterMap; the two dead components with live value (WorkflowTreeView, IncidentResolveDialog) are mounted where the persona needs them (incident record).

Anything that needs a new API field (reporter_name on Incident, creator name on Submission, actor_name on WorkflowEvent, office_name on Assessment, incident attachments list, per-incident assessment_id/state on Event Group detail, total_count on lists, workload on engineer options, cross sections attached to an assessment) is marked 'flag: backend' and omitted from the UI until it exists; nothing in this spec renames a backend field or changes a state transition.
